reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Attic perforation plus foul discharge equals cholesteatoma until disproven
Cholesteatoma is skin in middle ear eroding bone; surgery only cure
Central perforation is safe; marginal and attic are unsafe
Chronic ear plus vertigo or facial palsy means complication now
reference.pathophysiology: Negative middle ear pressure retracts the lax attic drum into a pocket that traps keratin, while enzymes and infected debris erode bone. Expanding keratin pearls destroy ossicles and can fistulise the labyrinth or expose dura.
additionalDifferentials: Safe versus unsafe CSOM by perforation site
Cholesteatoma versus canal keratosis or wax
Congenital cholesteatoma (intact drum) versus acquired retraction pocket
additionalInvestigations: CT temporal bone; diffusion weighted MRI for residual disease
